method.roles: Use source-disjoint news and abstracts for fit (first 24 works per genre) and calibration (next 16 each). Hold out essays entirely. Use the next 20 news and abstract works each as separate same-genre held groups if available. Use up to 48 unseen essay works.
method.selection: Select in fixed SHA-256 order. Exclude works in the previous paired news and abstract cohorts and any normalized 12-word overlap between admitted seeds or those excluded works. Each work must have one source-native five-sentence excerpt with exactly one annotated center from each of two generators. Use the unchanged source excerpt as a control. Use character offsets and inline tags for truth. Reject reviews with uncertain native offset mapping.
method.arms: Fit two source-balanced logistic heads. The first uses the primary classifier in isolation and in native three-sentence context. The second combines the same measurements from both checkpoints. For each checkpoint use isolated center, context, their difference, and each relative to the median across the interior sentences. Only the submitted excerpt enters inference.
method.fit: Weight each source equally and balance positive and negative truth per source. L2 coefficient .10, standard deviations floored at .1, 100 deterministic gradient steps at .3. Use separate points at the second-highest genuine calibration maximum per arm. Select at most one unique interior sentence.
method.baseline: Use the primary checkpoint's first six windows at .50, with its native edge windows. A useful range covers at least half of the labeled nonspace characters and reaches .30 intersection over union. Also count wrong candidate locations and ordinary false flags.
method.decision: An optional new confirmation hint needs at least four additional useful locations across both generators and at most two more flagged ordinary works than the incumbent on the essay holdout. A narrower presentation policy needs at least 75 percent of incumbent useful essay locations and at least three fewer ordinary works flagged. Neither can alter authorship confidence.
